title: TypeOp base-class getOutputLocal/getInputLocal defaults, TypeOpFunc metatype derivation, and TypeOpCall constructor opflags
status_note: Production commit bfba4b4 aligns the TypeOp trait local-type defaults with the Ghidra base class (getBase(size,TYPE_UNKNOWN), typeop.cc:261-275) through the shared base_local_type helper plus the local_type_factory provider hook, injects the factory into the four no-override opcodes (BRANCH/BRANCHIND/SEGMENTOP/CAST), and sets TypeOpCall::get_flags to the typeop.cc:663 opflags. The locked Ghidra 12.0.4 oracle and the frozen Rugra snapshot were each executed twice with deterministic stdout/stderr. Ghidra produced 102 records / 3560 bytes; Rugra produced 102 records / 3578 bytes. The covered projection (flags.call 8 lines, BRANCH/BRANCHIND/SEGMENTOP/CAST base defaults including the 3-byte unkbyte3 findAdd path, CALL no-FSPEC input/output through the TypeOp base defaults, and the CALL locked-parameter D1 regression) is byte-identical. The byte comparison is MISMATCH with 50 diff records / 1615 bytes: exactly 16 differing lines, all inside the four ZEXT/SEXT cases, where the oracle derives getBase(size,metain/metaout) (uint1/uint4/char/int4) while the current Rugra macro override returns the opposite varnode's v_type (xunknown4/xunknown1, sizes swapped) — the registered PRINTC-CAST-OPNAME-0001 M1 macro gap this fixture deliberately exposes as bilateral oracle evidence. Overall remains MISMATCH and this evidence cannot support L3.

bilateral_comparison.note: The locked Ghidra and Rugra stdout streams were byte-diffed with exit code 1; the only differing lines are the 16 ZEXT/SEXT result/meta/size/meta_identity lines inside the four metatype-derivation cases (PRINTC-CAST-OPNAME-0001 M1). All flags lines, all base-default cases, both CALL no-FSPEC cases, and the CALL locked-parameter case are byte-identical.

decisive_semantics.references_and_outputs: Ghidra base defaults are const methods reading only op->getOut()/getIn(slot) sizes and returning the canonical TypeFactory-owned Datatype* (repeated calls preserve pointer identity, verified by repeat_identity on both sides). TypeOpCall::getFlags returns the constructor opflags field (typeop.hh:72). Rugra returns canonical Arc clones from the same factory allocation via the local_type_factory provider; flags are a pure bit combination of op::pcodeop_flags constants.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_and_order: No loops anywhere in the observed functions: the defaults are single expressions, the ZEXT/SEXT derivation is a single getBase(size,meta) per side, and TypeOpCall::getInputLocal keeps its fixed guard order (slot 0 / non-annotation fallback, param slot-1, locked branch before this-pointer branch).
decisive_semantics.counters_and_accumulators: No counters. The only size source is the queried varnode itself (output: getOut()->getSize(); input: getIn(slot)->getSize()); the fixture pins 1/3/4/8-byte operands including the non-core 3-byte findAdd path.
decisive_semantics.sort_and_comparison_keys: No sorting. Decisive keys: the (size, TYPE_UNKNOWN) canonical intern for the defaults, (size, TYPE_UINT/TYPE_INT) for the TypeOpFunc derivation (meta_identity), the opflags bit set for CALL, and canonical pointer/Arc identity for every result and repeat observation.

residuals.note: M1 macro gap kept open by design: the binary/unary/functional macro overrides read the opposite varnode's v_type instead of getBase(size,metain/metaout). The 16 differing ZEXT/SEXT lines are the bilateral oracle evidence for M1; after M1 ports the metatype tables these lines must re-pin to MATCH.

Both R3 review gaps closed and bilaterally verified: trait defaults now perform the Ghidra base-class getBase(size,TYPE_UNKNOWN) lookup through the shared helper and factory provider hook, and TypeOpCall::get_flags returns the typeop.cc:663 opflags. CBRANCH/CALLIND/RETURN/CPOOLREF/NEW/CALLOTHER overrides and the CALL output-locked branch remain unported (kept as None / no factory, no false alignment).
